question: At least 56 Palestinians who have been awarded IUPALS, AFAM and Erasmus+ scholarships by Bologna, Milan, Calabria, Roma Tor Vergata and other Italian universities cannot leave the Gaza Strip owing to a lack of safe corridors and stalled consular procedures.

For these students – who hail from an area where all campuses have been completely destroyed – attending an EU university is the only chance they have of exercising the right to pursue an education enshrined in Article 14 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.

In the light of the fact that Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement makes relations between the two parties conditional on upholding human rights and that Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (known as the Visa Code) provides for procedural derogations and emergency measures for humanitarian cases and prospective students, we ask the Commission: 1.
What urgent steps involving the EEAS and the competent authorities will it take to facilitate the issuing of visas and the opening of educational corridors for the 56 students mentioned above?

How will the Commission work with the Member States to ensure that this bureaucratic inertia does not prevent Palestinians who have already been granted scholarships from making use of them before they expire?
How will the Commission ensure that the right to pursue an education is upheld in line with the Union’s external action policy objectives for conflict areas?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Cecilia Strada (S&D).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.5.2026) The Commission is fully aware of the extremely difficult circumstances facing Palestinian students in Gaza, including those who have been awarded scholarships under programmes such as Erasmus+ and through bilateral arrangements with European universities and are unable to leave Gaza.
The Commission is aware of evacuations of students from Gaza carried out by individual Member States, such as Spain and Italy.

The Commission, in close coordination with the European External Action Service and in particular through the Office of the European Union Representative (West Bank and Gaza Strip, United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees) and the National Erasmus+ Office in Palestine, has been engaging with Member States, relevant consular authorities, and international partners present in Palestine to explore possible avenues to facilitate the departure of Palestinian students from Gaza, notably those participating in EUfunded programmes and in bilateral arrangements with European universities.
